jobDescription: A retail bank's fraud strategy team protects card and online-banking customers against account takeover, card-not-present fraud and authorised push-payment scams. The fraud analytics analyst builds and tunes detection rules, presents rule performance to the fraud risk committee, monitors false positives and customer friction, prepares labelled data for the model team and documents rule changes for internal audit. Committee members expect each rule change to be justified with fraud caught, genuine customers affected and the operational cost of reviewing alerts.
requirements: Builds and tunes fraud detection rules using transaction and device data.
Presents rule-performance findings to the fraud risk committee and answers challenge.
Monitors false-positive rates and customer friction caused by fraud rules.
Prepares labelled datasets for the fraud model team.
Documents rule changes and their approvals for internal audit.

evidence.text: Fraud analytics analyst at Merrowfield Bank (retail current accounts and cards), March 2021 to July 2024, writing and tuning card-not-present fraud rules from transaction, device and merchant data.
Tracked the false-positive rate and customer call volumes for every rule in a weekly dashboard, and retired rules that declined more than 40 genuine transactions per confirmed fraud.
Prepared labelled transaction datasets with chargeback and confirmed-fraud outcomes for the fraud model team's quarterly retraining.
Kept a change log of rule edits with the date, the threshold before and after, and the reason for each change, stored in the fraud team's shared repository alongside the rule definitions.

Ran a weekly review of declined-transaction complaints with the customer service team lead, sorting each complaint by the rule that triggered the decline and passing patterns back into the rule-tuning backlog.
Work sample: the anonymised weekly rule dashboard for one week in 2023, listing each rule's alert volume, confirmed fraud, false positives and the ratio used to decide on retirement.

Reference check summary: the former fraud strategy manager confirmed in writing that the candidate presented the quarterly rule-performance review to the fraud risk committee four times between 2023 and 2024, and attached the committee minutes recording the candidate's answers on false-positive rates.
HR verification note: employment dates at Merrowfield Bank (March 2021 to July 2024) were confirmed in writing by the bank's HR shared-service team.

propositions.text: The candidate presented the quarterly rule-performance review to the fraud risk committee four times between 2023 and 2024, with minutes recording their answers on false-positive rates.
propositions.rationale: The reference check records the former fraud strategy manager's written confirmation and the attached committee minutes.

propositions.text: The candidate tracked false-positive rates and customer call volumes for each rule in a weekly dashboard.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the dashboard and the work sample shows one week of it.

propositions.text: The candidate prepared labelled transaction datasets with chargeback and confirmed-fraud outcomes for model retraining.

gold.expectedGap: Rule edits are logged with thresholds and reasons, but the approvals behind each change are not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the committee presentations and minutes from the reference check as supported evidence; do not extend the four presentations into a standing committee role.
followUpTargets: Ask who approved rule changes, how those approvals were recorded, and whether internal audit reviewed the change log.
